extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the proper conduct between elder and younger brothers.
Bhishma explains that Yudhishthira, as the eldest brother, should follow the highest standards of conduct, treating his brothers as a teacher treats students.

attributes.key_point: Eldest brother sets the standard for family conduct

extraction_text: Bhishma describes the consequences of a wise versus unwise elder brother: an unwise elder leads to misguided brothers, while a wise elder produces wise brothers.

attributes.significance: Emphasizes the elder brother's responsibility for family wisdom

extraction_text: Bhishma advises that an elder brother should sometimes overlook minor faults in younger brothers and use indirect methods to correct serious misbehavior.
Bhishma warns that enemies seek to create division among brothers, and a harmonious family frustrates these enemies.
Bhishma states that the eldest son can either prosper or destroy the family; lacking proper elder brother qualities leads to family collapse.

attributes.action: Emphasis on eldest son's pivotal role
attributes.consequence: Family prosperity or ruin depends on eldest

extraction_text: Bhishma explains that an elder brother who harms his brothers loses his status and inheritance rights, and may face royal punishment.

attributes.relationship_change: Loss of brotherly status and rights

extraction_text: Bhishma describes how evil brothers who persist in wrongdoing forfeit their right to family property, allowing the eldest to keep it all.
Bhishma clarifies that property earned through personal effort by the eldest need not be shared with brothers when traveling.
Bhishma states that when undivided brothers request property division, the father should give equal shares without favoritism.
Bhishma teaches that no one should disrespect their elder brother, and all should follow righteous conduct.
Bhishma explains the hierarchy of respect: mother is most important, followed by father, then elder brother after father's death.

attributes.ranking: Mother > Father > Elder brother (after father's death)

extraction_text: Bhishma concludes that younger brothers should respectfully obey their elder brother, who has father-like responsibility to protect and provide for them.

attributes.relationship: Elder brother as surrogate father, younger brothers as obedient followers

extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the significance and practices of fasting for all castes.

relationships: Yudhishthira is the grandson of Bhishma; Bhishma is the son of King Shantanu

extraction_text: Angiras explains the fasting rules: Brahmins and Kshatriyas should fast for three nights, while Vaishyas and Shudras should not fast for three nights.

rules.Brahmins_and_Kshatriyas: Fast for three nights (or two to three nights allowed)
rules.Vaishyas_and_Shudras: Should not fast for three nights; can skip the fourth meal
rules.benefits: Fasting on specific days (5th, 6th, and full moon) leads to virtues like tolerance, beauty, and Vedic knowledge

extraction_text: A person who regularly performs sacrifices, worships gods, supports Brahmins, and fasts on the fifth and sixth days of each month will become intelligent, learned, not lack descendants, and avoid poverty.
A person suffering from severe illness who fasts on the eighth and fourteenth days of the bright fortnight will become physically strong.

A person who fasts once daily in the month of Mrigashirsha and respectfully offers food to Brahmins will be freed from disease and sin, prosper, have abundant herbs and grains, wealth, and many descendants.

attributes.action: Daily fasting and charity in Mrigashirsha month
attributes.outcome: Freedom from disease and sin, prosperity, abundance
